To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the growth of a GaAlAs/GaAs heterojunction on vicinal (001) surfaces is a complex process, and that it is possible to control the lateral potential modulation by the electron gas screening and/or the tilt of the modulation.

the growth of quantum wires with strong in-plane potential modulation at short scale is feasible, that the growth conditions are crucial to obtain a good step array, and that the electron gas has a strong influence on the morphology of the surface.

the growth of a GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure on a (001) vicinal surface is a self-organizing process that results in a periodic modulation of the electron potential, and that the modulation amplitude can be tuned by the electron concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth and properties (structural, electronic, transport) of modulated electron structures on GaAs vicinals.
the understanding of the electronic and structural properties of modulated systems, in particular of quantum structures, grown on vicinal GaAs surfaces, in order to optimize the growth conditions.
the optimization of the epitaxial growth of modulated quantum structures, the understanding of their electronic properties and the development of a new generation of devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the modulation potential is not strongly affected by the screening of the electron gas, and that the effective potential is mainly due to the step edge barrier.
the growth of a 1D quantum wire is possible on GaAs vicinals, provided that the surface is well ordered and that the modulation period is short.

the growth of modulated quantum structures on GaAs vicinals requires the optimization of several parameters, such as the surface miscut, the temperature, the growth rate, the Al composition, and the electron density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the growth of the modulated structures is not limited by the morphology of the surface, that the electronic properties of the system can be controlled by the tilt of the modulation, and that the screening of the modulation potential by the 2DEG is not negligible.
the growth of quantum wires with strong lateral modulation can be achieved on vicinal GaAs(001) surfaces with a step density of 10 7 cm-1, a period of 20 nm and an amplitude of 100 meV. Proc. SPIE
the optimization of the epitaxy is a prerequisite to obtain the desired modulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth of a quantum well (QW) with an in-plane modulation of the potential can be optimized by using a vicinal substrate with a large miscut and a low temperature of growth.
the growth of a modulated electron system can be controlled and that its properties can be tailored by tuning the growth conditions.
the growth of quantum structures can be optimized through the use of vicinal substrates.
